evidence.quote: At today’s meeting, the Committee raised the target range for the federal funds rate by ¼ percentage point, bringing the target range to 4¾ to 5 percent.
we no longer state that we anticipate that ongoing rate increases will be appropriate to quell inflation; instead, we now anticipate that some additional policy firming may be appropriate.
participants don’t see rate cuts this year. They just don’t.
The process of getting inflation back down to 2 percent has a long way to go and is likely to be bumpy.
In principle, as a matter of fact, you can think of it as being the equivalent of a rate hike or perhaps more than that
obviously, at the end of the day, we will do enough to bring inflation down to 2 percent. No one should doubt that.

parsed.rationale: The Fed hiked 25bp, said inflation remains too high, and ruled out cuts this year. The hawkish signal is tempered by softening guidance from 'ongoing' to 'some additional firming may' and by the view that banking-related credit tightening could substitute for further hikes.
